standard_prerequisites: The divisor of a nonzero meromorphic section of an invertible sheaf and its flat pullback, together with the multiplicity of an irreducible component in a cycle

The construction of a torsor trivialising an invertible sheaf, the identification of the divisor of a meromorphic section with the divisor of the corresponding rational function on that torsor, and the behaviour of the divisors under the projection
The composition of flat pullbacks, and the rational function case of the formula for flat pullback of a principal divisor with multiplicities
core_obligations: Choose the torsor over the base trivialising the invertible sheaf and form the fibre product of that torsor with the source, so that the pullback of the sheaf to the fibre product is trivial
Reduce to the pulled back statement: since the projection to the source is a flat morphism of the relevant type, it suffices to prove the identity after pulling back along it
Identify the data on the fibre product: its irreducible components are the preimages of the components of the source, with the same multiplicities as the components of the source

Rewrite the left hand side using the identification of the divisor of a pulled back meromorphic section with the divisor of the corresponding rational function on the torsor, combined with the compatibility of flat pullback with composition
Rewrite the right hand side in the same way, component by component, using the same identification for the restricted morphisms to the components

Observe that under these identifications the pulled back sections become the compositions of the rational function on the torsor with the inclusions of its components, so that the identity is exactly the rational function formula for flat pullback of a principal divisor
proof_roadmap: Introduce the trivialising torsor and pull the whole problem back to the fibre product
Identify the components and multiplicities on the fibre product
Translate both sides into divisors of rational functions through the trivialisation
Recognise the resulting identity as the rational function case of the formula
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the flat pullback formula for the divisor of a meromorphic section at source lines 2734-2749, label lemma-prepare-flat-pullback-cap-c1, whose proof occupies source lines 2751-2800. The proof does not repeat the geometric work of the rational function case; instead it manufactures a situation in which the invertible sheaf becomes trivial, by taking a torsor over the base and pulling everything back along the flat projection from the fibre product. Everything then has to be identified: the components of the fibre product with those of the source and their multiplicities, the divisor of a pulled back meromorphic section with the divisor of the corresponding rational function, and the restricted pulled back sections with compositions of that rational function with the inclusions of the components, after which the identity is precisely the rational function formula. The counted statement records neither the torsor nor the identifications.
